card.keepWhy: Crown or forest, he received both the same way.
sources: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda (the second book): Ayodhya prepares for Rama’s crowning; Kaikeyi’s two boons; Rama is told he will go into exile for fourteen years; Sita and Lakshmana go with him
Ayodhya Kanda: Valmiki notes that Rama’s face showed no change on losing the kingdom (the film’s line)
Valmiki as the poet of the Ramayana (week-one lesson “The robber who became a poet”)
check: Exact verse where Valmiki says Rama showed no change on losing the kingdom (Ayodhya Kanda, around sarga 19: his glow undimmed, like the moon at night); confirm the reference. The best-known “lotus face neither brightened at the crowning nor faded at exile” verse is Tulsidas’s (Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, opening shloka 2), not Valmiki’s.
Today: saying “ram, ram” softly in hard moments, offered as a choice. Confirm it reads naturally to Hindu families.
Hard-one gloss: Ramayana as “Rama’s journey” (ayana: going, path, journey). Confirm wording.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? has a big plan of yours fallen through? a trip, a job, something you were counting on.
options: then this one is for you. listen.
then you’ll see this story from the other side.
good. keep this one for when it happens.

steps.line: It was supposed to be the best day of Rama’s life. The whole city of Ayodhya was decorated. Today, he would be crowned king.

steps.q: Rama’s crowning is about to be undone by two wishes the king once promised. Promised to whom?
steps.why: Kaikeyi once saved King Dasharatha in battle, and he owed her two wishes. She asked for her son Bharata to be crowned, and Rama sent to the forest for fourteen years.

steps.line: Instead, that morning, he was told: not king. Exile. Fourteen years in the forest.
And Valmiki, who wrote the Ramayana, notices one small detail: Rama’s face didn’t change. Crown or forest, he received both the same way.
steps.label: Ayodhya Kanda

steps.q: You’re Rama. Your father is broken by his promise and can barely speak. What do you do?
o: Ask the people of the city to decide
Go, so your father’s word is kept
Stay, and let your father break it
steps.why: In Valmiki’s telling, Rama goes so his father won’t be a man who broke his word. Truth, satya, mattered more to him than a crown.

steps.q: The Bhagavad Gita later names this kind of steadiness. What does it ask you to treat alike?
o: Friends and strangers, near and far
Pleasure and pain, gain and loss
Work and rest, day and night
steps.why: Gita 2.38: pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, alike. Many Hindus see Rama’s unchanged face as that verse lived out.

steps.q: Fourteen years in the forest. Does anyone go with him?
steps.why: Sita and Lakshmana. Neither was ordered to go. Sita refused to stay behind, and Lakshmana begged to come.

steps.line: He walked into the forest, with Sita and his brother Lakshmana beside him.

steps.q: Back in Ayodhya, Kaikeyi’s son Bharata is offered the throne. What does he do?
o: Takes the crown, as his mother wished
Puts Rama’s sandals on the throne
steps.why: Bharata refused to rule in Rama’s place. He set Rama’s sandals on the throne and ruled as caretaker for fourteen years.

steps.line: And the forest is where his real story happened.

say: here’s what i love. the worst morning of rama’s life is where his whole story begins.
hindus hold up rama’s steady face as the ideal: meet good news and bad news the same way, and keep walking the right path.

steps.q: Ramayana means “Rama’s journey.” From this lesson, why is that such a fitting name?
o: He journeyed to Ayodhya to be crowned
He left home and never came back
The road he never planned became his story
steps.why: No forest, no Ramayana. The plan that fell apart became the journey everyone remembers.

today.say: today, when news comes, good or bad, try rama’s way: one breath before you react, and meet it the same. many hindus say rama’s name softly in hard moments, “ram, ram.” you can join in, or just breathe. it’s your choice.
options: good. crown or forest, one breath first.
that’s okay. everyone around rama fell apart too. give it time.
